issues.detail: The Hebrew 'אֹיְבִ֥י כִלָּֽם' means 'my enemy has consumed/annihilated them' (the enemy is the subject of the verb, consuming the ones I raised). The Chinese renders it as '祂已盡滅其敵' ('He has completely destroyed His enemies'), reversing the subject and object: in Hebrew, the enemy destroys the nurtured ones, not God destroying the enemy. This changes who is doing what to whom.
